lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Algorithms and Robots
lesson.summary: Giving a robot directions, algorithms, loops, if-then and finding bugs.
learning_objectives: Say what an algorithm, a loop and a bug are
Fix a mistake in a set of instructions

standards.text: Understand what algorithms are; create and debug simple programs
Model daily processes by creating and following algorithms
Develop programs with sequences and simple loops
Debug errors in an algorithm or program

success_criteria: I can put steps in the right order
I can say what a loop does
I can find and fix a bug
lesson.real_life: Cooking rice, making chai and getting ready for school all follow steps in order.

warm_up.prompt: Which comes next? Red, blue, red, blue, ...
warm_up.explanation: The pattern repeats red then blue.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how do we give clear steps?
blocks.say: Today we learn how to tell a robot exactly what to do.

blocks.alt: Two slices of white bread on a dark table
blocks.caption: Even a sandwich needs steps in order.
blocks.credit: Photo by Graphy Co on Unsplash
blocks.say: These two slices of bread are the start of a sandwich. Steps matter.

blocks.markdown:
A robot does exactly what we tell it. These are **instructions**.

**Forward** moves one square. **Turn** changes the way it faces.
blocks.say: Meet our robot. It cannot think for itself. It only does exactly what we tell it, one instruction at a time. The robot wants to reach the star in the corner. We can say forward, to move one square. Or turn, to face a new way. Watch the robot walk along the top row.

blocks.title: The robot walks to the star

scenes.caption: The robot starts in the top corner.
scenes.say: Here is the robot at the start. The star is far away in the opposite corner. The robot faces right.

scenes.caption: Forward, forward again.
scenes.say: Forward, forward again. Now the robot is in the top right corner.

scenes.caption: Turn to face down.
scenes.say: Now turn. The robot turns to face down, ready to walk to the star.

scenes.caption: Forward four times and we reach the star!
scenes.say: Forward four times, and the robot reaches the star! Well done, robot.

question.prompt: Which instruction moves the robot one square?
question.explanation: Forward moves the robot one square along.

blocks.markdown:
An **algorithm** is a list of clear steps in the right **order**.

Muddle the order and it does not work!
blocks.say: A list of clear steps, in the right order, is called an algorithm. You use algorithms every day without noticing. Think about making a sandwich. First the bread, then the cheese, then the top slice. If we muddle the order, we get a very silly sandwich!

scenes.caption: 1. Bread on the plate.
scenes.say: Step one. Put the bread on the plate.

scenes.caption: 2. Add the cheese.
scenes.say: Step two. Add the cheese on top of the bread.

scenes.caption: 3. Top slice on. Yum!
scenes.say: Step three. Put the top slice on. Now it is a sandwich! The order mattered.

question.prompt: Put these steps for washing your hands in order.
question.explanation: We wet our hands, then use soap, then rinse and dry.

blocks.title: Zainab and the robot
blocks.transcript: Zainab has a toy robot. It only follows exact steps. She says forward, forward. The robot moves two squares. Then turn. The robot now faces the star. Oh no! The robot stops short. One forward is missing. Zainab adds one more forward. That is called debugging. Now she uses a loop. Repeat forward four times. The robot reaches the star. Clear steps in order worked. Zainab uses steps to make a sandwich too. Order matters!
blocks.caption: Zainab gives a robot exact steps and fixes a bug.

points: Instructions tell a robot what to do
An algorithm is clear steps in the right order
blocks.say: Let us remember. Instructions tell a robot what to do. An algorithm is a list of clear steps in the right order.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Doing it again with a loop

blocks.markdown: A **loop** repeats instructions. Instead of hop, hop, hop, say: repeat hop 3 times.
blocks.say: Sometimes a robot must do the same thing again and again. We could say forward, forward, forward, forward. That is a lot of words! Instead we can say repeat forward four times. A set of instructions that repeats is called a loop. Watch the frog hop three times using one loop.

scenes.caption: Start.
scenes.say: The frog starts on the log.

scenes.caption: Hop 1.
scenes.say: Hop number one. Our loop says: repeat hop, three times.

scenes.caption: Hop 2.
scenes.say: Hop number two. The same instruction again.

scenes.caption: Hop 3. The loop is done.
scenes.say: Hop number three. The loop is finished!

question.prompt: A loop says: repeat clap, 4 times. How many claps is that?

blocks.title: Be the robot loop
instructions: Ask your friend to say: repeat jump, 3 times.
Do the loop exactly: jump, jump, jump.
Now swap. Can you make up a loop with clap and stamp?

blocks.markdown:
**If** something is true, **then** do something.

If it is raining, then take an umbrella.
blocks.say: Computers make choices too. They use the words if and then. If it is raining, then take an umbrella. If it is sunny, then wear a hat. The computer checks the question first, and then chooses what to do.

blocks.alt: A rain cloud and an umbrella.
blocks.caption: If it is raining, then take an umbrella.

question.prompt: If the light is red, then the car must...
question.explanation: If the light is red, then the car stops.

points: If this, then that helps a computer choose
blocks.say: Let us remember. A loop repeats instructions. If-then lets a computer choose what to do.

terms.meaning: A set of instructions that repeats.
To do the same thing again.
A word that asks a question before we choose.
A word that tells what to do next.

blocks.markdown:
A **bug** is a mistake in the instructions.

**Debugging** means finding and fixing the bug.
blocks.say: Sometimes our instructions have a mistake. A mistake in instructions is called a bug. Finding and fixing a bug is called debugging. Look at this robot. We told it forward, forward, forward, forward, then turn. But the star is in the corner. The robot stopped before it got there. Where is the bug?

scenes.caption: Three forwards only.
scenes.say: The robot follows: forward, forward, forward. That is only three steps.

scenes.caption: One forward is missing. That is the bug!
scenes.say: It needed four steps to reach the corner. The star is still far away. The bug is that one forward is missing.

scenes.caption: Add one forward. Bug fixed!
scenes.say: We add one more forward. Now the robot reaches the corner. We fixed the bug!

question.prompt: A robot must go forward 3 steps but only goes 2. What is the bug?
question.explanation: The instructions are missing one forward.

blocks.markdown: Watch carefully, then copy the **order** of the lights.
blocks.say: Time for a brain game. Watch the lights, then copy them in the same order. Remembering the order is just like following an algorithm.

blocks.markdown: We follow **algorithms** at home: making chai, cooking rice, getting ready for school.
blocks.say: Algorithms are not only for robots. People follow them all the time. Getting ready for school has steps. So does making a cup of chai, or cooking rice, or tidying a room. If you do the steps in order, the job works. What other algorithms can you think of at home?

blocks.caption: Cooking rice, making chai and packing a school bag all have steps in order.

blocks.markdown: Write your own **algorithm**. Then test it on a grown-up. If it goes wrong, **debug** it!
blocks.say: Now it is your turn to be the programmer. Choose a job, like making a sandwich or tidying the toys. Write the steps in order, or draw them. Then ask a grown-up to follow only your steps, exactly. If they get stuck, you found a bug!

blocks.alt: Write the steps, then test them.
blocks.caption: Write the steps, then test them.
blocks.say: Write the steps down or draw them. Then test them.

blocks.title: My own algorithm
instructions: Choose a job, such as making a sandwich.
Draw or write each step in order.
Ask a grown-up to follow your steps exactly.
Did it work? If not, find the bug and fix it.
blocks.say: Now you try. Follow the steps on the card. Take your time.

blocks.prompt: Could you give a robot the steps for brushing teeth?
blocks.answer_markdown: Yes! Put paste on the brush, brush the front, brush the back, rinse. A robot would need every tiny step.
blocks.say: Have a think. Could you give a robot the steps for brushing teeth? Tap to find out.
